transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It’s really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um, well, I guess what brought me in is... I just don't really feel like myself anymore? I hope that’s an okay way to explain it. I don't want to make a big fuss or anything, but... I’ve noticed I barely talk to people lately. I just sort of go, well, flat and quiet. And at work—I clean buildings—even just getting started on my cleaning route, it feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. I mean, I still get the job done, I always try to be a good worker, but it's just been a lot harder. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Um, depressed? Well... I don't think I'd use that word, exactly. I really try to stay positive, you know? I have a steady job and a roof over my head, so I definitely don't want to sound ungrateful or like I'm complaining. 

I guess maybe I just feel a little... worn out? Like I was saying, just a bit tired. But I'm still trying my best every day to keep a good attitude. I hope it's okay to say that. I just wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, giving up or anything like that. Does that sound like an okay answer?
Have you been feeling sad or down most days?

Well, um... sad? I don't know if I'd say sad, exactly. I mean, sure, maybe some days I feel a little low, but doesn't everybody? I really try to just keep my chin up and focus on the good things. I don't want to sit around feeling sorry for myself, you know? 

I guess I just don't want to make it sound worse than it is. I'm still getting up and going to work, and I try to be friendly to folks when I see them. Is it normal to just feel a little... flat sometimes? I hope I'm explaining this right. I just really want to be helpful and give you the right answers.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot?

Oh, worrying? Um, no, I don't think I'm much of a worrier, really. I always try to just take things as they come. 

I mean, sure, I care about doing things right—I want to make sure I do a good job on my floors and everything—but I don't sit around fretting or letting things get to me. I really try not to be a bother to anyone with a bunch of nervous energy, you know? I just like to keep my head down and do what I'm supposed to do. 

I hope that's an okay answer for you? I just don't want you to think I'm holding anything back, I just really don't find myself stressing over things too much.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Well... lose interest? I guess... maybe a little bit? But I really don't want it to sound like I'm just sitting around doing nothing, you know? I still try to keep busy. 

It's just... well, I used to really look forward to going fishing on Saturdays, or just sitting down with a cup of coffee and a crossword puzzle. And at work, I used to get a kick out of showing the younger guys some tricks for stripping a floor right. But lately... I don't know, I guess I just sort of let those things sit. It's not that I hate them or anything! It's just that they don't seem to give me that same... feeling back, if that makes sense? 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or unappreciative of my time off. I just haven't had the energy for the extra stuff. Is that... does that answer what you were asking?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, um... how long? I guess... it's been a little while now. But I really don't want to make a big fuss out of it, you know? It's not like I've been totally useless this whole time. 

If I really think about it, I suppose it's been building up for about... maybe a year and five months? Give or take? It kind of started around the time I had to move out of my old apartment and leave that neighborhood. I just haven't quite felt like myself since then. But I've still been getting to work and doing my job! I just... I guess the spark hasn't been there for a bit. 

Does that timeline make sense to you? I hope I'm giving you the right details. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you felt this flat or low most days without a break for nearly two years?

Well... two years? No, no, I wouldn't say it's been quite that long. I don't want you to think I've just been dragging my feet for two whole years, really. 

I guess the... the really low part, the feeling flat and down... that's been more like, um, a year and two months? Yeah, about a year and two months. It really kicked in shortly after I had to move. But I've still been trying my best to keep a smile on at work, you know? I really try not to let it show too much. 

I hope that's the right answer for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline, I don't want to make things sound worse than they are.
Did these changes start after you had to move out of your old apartment?

Well... yeah, I guess that's right. The move... that's when it really started to get noticeable. But I don't want to blame it all on the move, you know? It's not like I'm holding a grudge against the new place or anything. It's a perfectly fine apartment, really. 

It's just... leaving the old neighborhood, the routine I had... I think it just threw me off balance a bit. And then the low feelings just sort of crept in after that. But I'm adjusting! I really am trying to make the best of it. 

Does that make sense, though? That a move could sort of trigger this kind of thing? I just hope I'm not making excuses for myself.
Would you say these feelings have been stronger than you’d expect just from having to move?

Well, um... stronger? I don't know if I'd say stronger. I really don't want it to sound like I'm falling apart over a simple change of address, you know? Moving is a hassle for anybody. 

I mean, I'm still getting up and doing my cleaning shifts at the building every day, so it's not like I can't handle things. I guess maybe... it's just taking me a little longer to bounce back this time around. But I wouldn't say it's completely out of proportion or anything like that. 

Do you think that's a normal way to react? I just want to be sure I'm answering you right, I really don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill if this is just regular stress.
Before this started after the move, had you ever had another period in your life when you felt this same kind of low, flat, low-energy way for at least a couple of weeks?

Um... before the move? No, I... I really don't think so. I mean, everybody has a bad week here and there, right? Especially just getting older and working on your feet all day, you get a little tired. 

But... no, not this flat. I've always been a pretty steady guy. I always take pride in being reliable for my shifts, just keeping my head down and doing a good job. So this... this kind of slump, it's really the first time it's stuck around like this. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm trying to give you the most accurate history I can, I just... I've usually been pretty upbeat before all this. Is it normal for something like this to just happen for the first time at my age?
If you hadn’t had to move out of your old apartment, do you think you would still have started feeling this way?

Oh, gosh... that's a tough one. I mean... I'd like to think that if I hadn't had to pack up and leave, I'd still just be humming along, doing my job like always. Because my routine was so set over there, you know? 

But... I really couldn't say for sure. I don't want to sound like I'm just looking for a scapegoat. It's really not the new building's fault I'm in this kind of slump, so I don't want to just blame the move entirely. 

So... I guess I really don't know. Do you think it was bound to happen anyway, even if I'd stayed put? I hope it's okay that I don't have a solid answer for you on that one, I'm just trying not to jump to conclusions.
During this past year, have you felt down or depressed most of the day on most days?

Well, um... most of the day, on most days? I... I don't think I'd put it quite like that. I mean, a whole year is a long time, and I really wouldn't want to make it sound like I've just been moping around non-stop. 

I've been going to work, you know? Getting my cleaning done. So I definitely have good parts of the day where I'm just focused on the job. It's not like I'm just sitting in the dark all the time. 

I guess... maybe I've been a little more quiet than usual lately, but I wouldn't say I've been depressed *most* of the time. Does that sound right to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a fair picture, and not making it sound worse than it really is. I try to stay positive when I can.
Since this started, have you been waking up much earlier than usual and unable to get back to sleep?

Um... no, not really. I mean, my sleep hasn't been perfect, but I wouldn't say I'm waking up super early and just staring at the ceiling or anything. 

Sometimes I might wake up a little before my alarm, but I think that's just... you know, my body getting used to the schedule, or maybe just getting a little older. I usually just kind of rest my eyes until it's time to get up for my shift. I always make sure I get enough rest so I can do a good job at work. 

So, no, I don't think I've had that problem. Is it okay that my sleep is mostly normal? I hope I'm being helpful, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.
Since this started, have you noticed your appetite being a lot less than usual?

Well, um... maybe just a little bit. I really don't want you to think I'm not taking care of myself, because I know eating right is important. It's just... lately, I don't know, most days food just kind of tastes like cardboard to me. 

So I guess I might skip a meal here and there, or I'll just have a few crackers when I get home after my shift. I did notice my work pants have been hanging a bit looser than they used to, but... I'm still making sure I eat *something*, you know? I'm not trying to starve myself or anything. 

I hope it's alright that my appetite is a little off right now. Is it okay to just lose your taste for things like that, or is that something I should be doing better with?
Have you lost weight since this started?

Well, um... yeah, like I was just mentioning with my work pants being a bit loose, I guess I probably have lost a few pounds. I haven't actually stepped on a scale or anything, mostly because I didn't want to make a big deal out of it or worry anybody. 

But I suppose with the way food hasn't been appealing, and just having those crackers instead of a full dinner... the weight just kind of came off on its own. I really hope that's not too alarming. I'm still strong enough to do all my mopping and heavy lifting at work, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm letting myself go. 

Is it... is it okay that I've dropped a little weight, as long as I'm still getting my job done alright?
Over this past year, have you been feeling hopeless?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't use a strong word like hopeless. I know things can get tough, but I always try to look on the bright side, you know? 

Sometimes I get a little down, maybe feel like I'm just going through the motions with my cleaning routine... but I still get up and go to work every day. I know I have a job to do, and I want to do it well. I don't want to sit around feeling sorry for myself or anything like that. 

So, no, I wouldn't say hopeless. I hope that's the right kind of answer. I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I'm doing. Is it normal to just feel a little... flat sometimes, without it being a big problem?
Since this started, have you been feeling like you’re not as good or worthwhile as you used to be?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I feel completely worthless, you know? I mean, I still have my job and I work hard at it. But... I guess sometimes I do get these thoughts that I've let people down. 

Like... well, I lost my old place a while back, and I just feel like I didn't keep my life together the way I should have. And sometimes, it's silly, but if the church pantry is short on supplies, or even if a hallway just gets missed at work... my mind kind of jumps to thinking it's my fault somehow. Like I should have done more, or I'm just not doing enough. 

But I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in self-pity or anything! I know I'm still a good worker. It's just... those guilty feelings kind of creep up on me sometimes. I hope it's okay to admit that. Is it normal to feel a little extra responsible for things like that when you're going through a rough patch?
Since this started, have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Well, um... I don't want to worry you or make it sound like I'm, you know, in danger or anything. I don't have any kind of big plan to do anything bad. I really don't. 

But... I guess sometimes, when things are just feeling really heavy... a lot of mornings I wake up and just think, maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up at all. Just to rest, you know? Not have to worry about the cleaning or the bills or where I'm going to sleep. 

It actually scares me a bit to even say that out loud. I know it's not a good way to think, and I try to push those thoughts away as soon as they come. I really do want to keep going and do my job well. I hope you don't think less of me for admitting that. Is it... is it pretty common for people to have thoughts like that when they're just feeling a bit overwhelmed?
